scope: Local, free/local portfolio monitoring only -- not a commercial monitoring platform. No live customer telemetry, no paid service, no cloud infrastructure.

rules.calculation: Population Stability Index (PSI) between a batch's TransactionAmt decile distribution and the train-partition reference decile distribution.
rules.reference_source: train partition (438,125 rows), real values via src.preprocessing.load_partition_df -- never from an imputer median alone.
rules.threshold_rationale: Conventional PSI literature heuristic (<0.1 no significant shift, 0.1-0.25 moderate, >0.25 significant). This is a statistical-adequacy convention, NOT derived from Stage 1's cost scenarios and NOT claimed to be economically optimal -- no operational evidence exists yet to justify a cost-optimal threshold.
rules.expected_false_alert_limitations: A real, legitimate seasonal or promotional shift in transaction amounts would also trigger this alert -- PSI cannot distinguish 'malicious/erroneous data change' from 'genuine population change'. Small batches (near the 50-row minimum) will have noisier bin proportions and a higher false-alert rate than large batches.
rules.operator_response: See docs/STAGE18_MONITORING_RUNBOOK.md -- investigate upstream source/schema change before trusting new predictions.

rules.calculation: PSI between a batch's C1 decile distribution and the train-partition reference decile distribution.
rules.reference_source: train partition, real values. C1 chosen because it is Stage 11's top-ranked SHAP feature -- a drift here is the single most consequential input-drift signal this project can monitor given existing evidence.
rules.threshold_rationale: Same PSI convention as TransactionAmt -- a statistical heuristic, not a cost-derived figure.
rules.expected_false_alert_limitations: C1 is an anonymised Vesta-engineered count-like feature with unknown real-world units (Stage 2) -- a PSI alert can say THAT its distribution shifted, never WHY in business terms.

rules.calculation: PSI between a batch's dist1 decile distribution (computed over FINITE values only) and the train-partition reference decile distribution.
rules.reference_source: train partition, real values. dist1 chosen deliberately for its real, legitimate ~61.44% missingness (Stage 16 finding) -- exercises missing-value handling against real data.
rules.threshold_rationale: Same PSI convention. Missingness itself is tracked as a separate count (n_missing_or_non_finite), never folded into the PSI calculation or silently imputed.
rules.expected_false_alert_limitations: A change in the UPSTREAM MISSINGNESS RATE itself (e.g. a new data source that always populates dist1) would not be caught by this PSI rule, since PSI here is computed over finite values only -- a named, separate gap, not a claim of complete coverage.

rules.calculation: PSI between a batch's fraud_probability decile distribution (scored by the current trusted artifact, no refit) and a reference score distribution built the same way.
rules.reference_source: A reference batch sampled from the train partition and scored once by artifact sha256 2fb0cbc4... (Stage 13). Comparison is refused (status=provenance_mismatch) if the batch was scored by a different artifact checksum.
rules.threshold_rationale: Same PSI convention, applied to scores instead of a raw feature. fraud_probability is explicitly NOT a calibrated real-world probability (Stage 10/14) -- this rule monitors distribution SHAPE only, never a classification-accuracy claim.
rules.expected_false_alert_limitations: A score-distribution shift can be caused by an input-distribution shift (check the input_drift_* rules for the same batch first), by the batch's own composition (e.g. an unusually fraud-heavy real batch), or by a genuine model-behavior change -- this rule alone cannot distinguish the three.
rules.operator_response: See docs/STAGE18_MONITORING_RUNBOOK.md -- cross-check input_drift_* alerts for the same batch before concluding the MODEL itself changed behavior.

rules.calculation: count(HTTP status in [500,599]) over log records carrying both a status and duration_seconds field.
rules.reference_source: The existing Stage 14 `_log_event` structured log lines (parsed from a log file; Uvicorn's own plain-text access-log lines are skipped, not parsed as records).
rules.threshold_rationale: ANY observed 5xx is flagged, not a rate threshold. With the low request volume expected of a local portfolio API, waiting for a RATE to accumulate would hide the very first real outage -- deliberately more sensitive than a production-scale error-rate rule would need to be.
rules.expected_false_alert_limitations: A single transient 5xx (e.g. during an intentional redeploy, as in Stage 17's own Version B exercise) will always alert -- this rule cannot distinguish 'a real incident' from 'an expected, operator-initiated deployment transition'; the runbook's first step (observe and verify) exists specifically to make that distinction by hand.
rules.operator_response: See docs/STAGE18_MONITORING_RUNBOOK.md -- check /health and /version immediately; roll back per docs/STAGE17_ROLLBACK_RUNBOOK.md if the release is unready.

rules.calculation: set(artifact_sha256 values seen in successful-response log records) minus {approved_artifact_sha256}.
rules.threshold_rationale: Serving predictions from an unapproved artifact is always significant on this project's own terms (Stage 13's permanent checksum-identity contract) -- no rate threshold is appropriate.
rules.expected_false_alert_limitations: Only checked on SUCCESSFUL responses, because error responses never log artifact identity (a real, audited gap in the existing Stage 14 logging -- see docs/STAGE18_MONITORING_REPORT.md Section 2). A run of pure failures could theoretically be serving a bad artifact without this rule ever seeing it.
rules.operator_response: See docs/STAGE18_MONITORING_RUNBOOK.md -- verify which release is actually running; roll back if it is not the approved Version A.

rules.calculation: 95th percentile of duration_seconds over log records with a sufficient sample (>=20).
rules.reference_source: Stage 14's own measured warm p95 (0.0462s), from docs/STAGE14_API_REPORT.md.
rules.threshold_rationale: Deliberately set far above (~20x) Stage 14's measured warm p95, so this fires only on a real, large regression, not routine jitter from a single-worker local process under this stage's own small demonstration batches.
rules.expected_false_alert_limitations: A single slow request immediately after a cold start would not by itself cross a 95th-percentile threshold with a reasonably sized batch, but could with a very small one -- hence the 20-record minimum sample size.
rules.operator_response: See docs/STAGE18_MONITORING_RUNBOOK.md -- not evidence of model correctness decay; investigate for resource contention.
